slides.title: Careless AI Use Carries Real Consequences
bullets: Generative AI use in Medical Affairs is not risk-free
Consequences can reach confidential information and scientific credibility
Unlike a minor typo, these risks can cause lasting damage
Every MSL must know these risks precisely before daily use

slides.title: Hallucination Is Still the Most Cited Risk
bullets: Models can generate plausible, well-written but factually wrong content
Includes invented figures or references that do not exist
Especially dangerous when communicated confidently to an HCP
Retrieval-Augmented Generation anchors answers in verified sources
Even with RAG, final human verification against the original stays essential

slides.title: Privacy and Information Security
bullets: Prompt data can be stored or used to train future models
Never enter confidential company data or unpublished study results
Never enter identifiable patient information
Never enter identifiable HCP data without explicit consent and safeguards
Equivalent protections to HIPAA in the US or GDPR in Europe apply

slides.title: Algorithmic Bias in Model Training Data
bullets: Models learn from text that can reflect existing biases
Can underrepresent certain patient populations or clinical perspectives
Same critical thinking on representativeness as evidence gaps in Module 7

slides.title: A Governance Framework, Not Avoidance
bullets: Know and follow internal policy on approved tools and privacy settings
Never enter confidential or patient information
Always verify clinical claims against the primary source before sharing
The MSL keeps final professional responsibility for everything shared

takeaway.title: Hallucination, privacy, and bias are manageable risks under a clear governance framework
bullets: Hallucination is mitigated by RAG but still needs human verification
Confidential and patient data must never enter an AI prompt
Final professional responsibility for shared information stays with the MSL
